name: GNOME Boxes
issue: Snap's confinement commonly blocks the KVM/libvirt device access GNOME Boxes needs to run virtual machines — real, widely-reported "No KVM" errors even when KVM is available on the host.
fix: Try connecting the snap's virtualization interfaces first: sudo snap connect gnome-boxes:kvm && sudo snap connect gnome-boxes:libvirt — if that doesn't resolve it, installing via Flatpak or your distro's native package is the more reliable option.
reason: Verified live (2026-08-25): widely reported across GitHub/GitLab issue trackers and distro forums (flathub/org.gnome.Boxes#99, GNOME Boxes gitlab#1134, multiple Linux Mint/Fedora forum threads). Snapcraft does publish real kvm/libvirt interfaces for this exact purpose, but couldn't confirm live whether gnome-boxes' own snap manifest auto-connects them — command given as the standard troubleshooting step, not a guaranteed one-line fix.

name: Boxes
issue: May show a "No KVM" error even when KVM is available on the host — Flatpak's sandbox defaults libvirt to a URI the bundled qemu/libvirt can't reach.
reason: Verified live (2026-08-25): real, documented fix from flathub/org.gnome.Boxes#99 and confirmed working across multiple independent reports. Lower severity than the Snap entry since this one has a specific, confirmed-working one-line fix rather than just a workaround.
